designConstraints: Must not consume excessive context (router itself must be lightweight)
Must not require Codex to memorize all pages (router points, doesn't contain)
Must work with existing Context OS and startup verification
Must be verifiable: proof-of-read must have machine-readable evidence
Must not become a 'read everything' tax that blocks productive work

components.description: Factory MANIFEST maps phase/task to required reading pages. Router reads MANIFEST, not all pages.
Before each phase/task, verifier checks that required pages from MANIFEST were accessed (file read timestamp or hash-based proof)
SHA256 of read content logged to agent event ledger. Verifier confirms content hash matches expected.
Each phase declares max pages to read. Exceeding budget is a risk signal.

contextCostEstimate: Router MANIFEST: ~500 bytes. Read-event log per file: ~100 bytes. Total overhead per phase: <2KB. Negligible compared to project context.
whatAlreadyExists: Agent event ledger — can log read events
recommendation: BUILD MANUAL ROUTER FIRST (FACTORY-EVAL-2). Without proof-of-read, role-specialized agents cannot reliably read their role definitions, and verifier cannot confirm content comprehension.
problem: Codex may skip reading artifacts. Verifier checks file existence, not content comprehension. No mechanism ensures Codex read what it claims to have read.
whatNeedsBuilding: MANIFEST router mapping phase/task to required pages
